basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 14.' and it opens 'Vers. 14. Protinus eductum de carcere totonderunt. Eductio Joseph de carcere resurrectio'. The chapter is Migne's caput, carried from the last one the printing states, and the lemma raises nothing against it.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text: Vers. 14. Protinus eductum de carcere totonderunt. Eductio Joseph de carcere resurrectio est Christi, per quam omnem mortalitatem et infirmitatem quasi capillorum excrementa projecit, et vestem immortalitatis ac jucunditatis accepit.
